question.text: Aravalli Long-Short Fund incurred a business loss of INR 12 crore in FY2024-25 from derivatives (non-speculative). In FY2025-26 the fund earned business income of INR 9 crore from F&O and LTCG of INR 6 crore from listed equities. Under Sections 72 and 74 of the ITA, how can the loss be set off?

answer.text: INR 9 crore set off against F&O business income; remaining INR 3 crore carried forward as business loss (not against capital gains)
INR 12 crore set off against F&O INR 9 crore + LTCG INR 3 crore = zero taxable income
INR 12 crore fully carried forward; no set-off this year
INR 6 crore set off against LTCG only; balance INR 6 crore lapses

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Non-speculative business loss (Section 72) can be set off against any head in the year of loss (Section 71) subject to rules, but when CARRIED FORWARD can only be set off against BUSINESS income of subsequent years. It cannot be set off against capital gains when carried forward. So 9 cr of business loss offsets F&O gain; 3 cr is carried forward further. LTCG of 6 cr remains taxable at 12.5% minus exemption. **The Trap:** A wrongly offsets carried-forward business loss against LTCG. C says no set-off is allowed — wrong, Section 72 clearly permits against business income. D reverses head-matching rules. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-D tests the same mechanics for Cat I/II. XIX-E highlights it's done at the FUND level because there is no 115UB pass-through of loss. LP-level set-off (as in Cat I/II) does NOT apply. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** At Aravalli, carry-forward business loss is a fund-level asset — don't let it expire (8 years under Section 72). Right-size F&O exposure in the low-LTCG-only years to maximise set-off consumption before the clock runs out.
